verdicts.verify_by: cp tests/b1-lines-removed-reach-catalog-budget-at-cgroup-limit_test.go gno.land/pkg/integration/zz_budget_at_cgroup_limit_test.go && go test ./gno.land/pkg/integration -run TestReproBudgetAtCgroupLimit -v -count=1: the 0-byte row keeps limit 6 and reads 20 times in 20 polls, the 1-byte row cuts to 4 with 0 reads
verdicts.tldr: In a cgroup at its memory.max the node budget never shrinks and re-reads memory on every poll, so test nodes keep being admitted into a full cgroup.
verdicts.details: clampToCgroup (tm2/pkg/testutils/parallel_linux.go:71-79) sets free to 0 when used >= limit, so Available becomes 0, and ReadMemInfo then returns `mi, mi.Total > 0 && mi.Available > 0` (line 62), which is ok=false. resize (testscript_gnoland.go:215-217) does `if !ok { return }` before the shrink case and before `b.lastCheck = now`. A suite running in a container or systemd slice whose budget ramped while memory was free therefore keeps its ramped limit once the cgroup fills, handing every released slot to a waiter, and every blocked script's 200ms poll re-reads /proc/meminfo and the cgroup files. The finder's mock copies line 62's expression verbatim; the read of clampToCgroup confirms the real reader produces exactly that 0. Fix: treat a cgroup at its limit as a valid reading of Available 0 (return ok on Total > 0 alone, or report the clamp separately), so resize shrinks, and advance lastCheck before the read so a failed read is paced too.
verdicts.evidence: Head 115d118 in a scratch worktree, go1.25.9, go test ./gno.land/pkg/integration -run TestReproBudgetAtCgroupLimit -v -count=1: 'available=1 bytes: limit=4 (started 6, min 2), reads during 20 polls inside the interval=0' / 'available=0 bytes: limit=6 (started 6, min 2), reads during 20 polls inside the interval=20', PASS.
